newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Denktash blames Greek Cypriots, EU for failure.
newsitem.headline: Denktash blames Greek Cypriots, EU for failure.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on Friday accused the European Union and Greek Cypriots of causing talks on Cyprus unity to fail.
He said the Greek Cypriots had blocked an agreement by refusing to give Turks sovereign equality on the divided island.
In the meantime, he said, the EU threw in a bombshell with a decision to start entry talks early next year for the Greek Cypriot government.
Greece is a member of the 15-nation EU, Turkey is not.

"The failure of the talks was clear from the beginning. I think we all knew in a few meetings that the solution would not appear," he told a news conference after the five-day round in the village of Glion, near Montreux, ended.
Denktash said no further round had been fixed, but U.N. mediator Diego Cordovez would issue a statement on the continuation of the process.

Diplomats said Cordovez read the text of the statement to both leaders from a hand-written paper while they took notes during their closed-door meeting. Denktash accepted the statement while Clerides had raised objections, they added.
Sources close to Clerides said that he continued to negotiate the wording long after Denktash had ended their talks.
Its final wording was still not known, although Cordovez has scheduled a final news conference for 4:30 p.m. (1430 GMT) in Montreux.

Denktash, holding a hand-written draft of the statement, quoted it as referring to "useful discussions in Troutbeck, New York, and Glion, with both sides committed to a bizonal and bicommunal settlement".

He said the statement would contain a provision that Cordovez would visit Cyprus, divided since 1974 when Turkey invaded the north in response to a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.

The statement would refer to wide-ranging dicussions on various issues and say the process initiated by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan will continue, Denktash said. Discussions on humanitarian issues would also carry on.
Denktash said the meeting had been useful for both sides in understanding each others' positions as well as for Cordovez, whom he described as a "newcomer".
He said he was pleased with the final U.N. statement.

He quoted Cordovez as saying "his mandate is to see that the process is not destroyed". "I agree with him but I told him that we have to wait until the end of the year to see what the EU decides to do with Cyprus," the Turkish Cypriot leader said.
Denktash reiterated there would be no furhter round until EU makes its position clear.
"The Cyprus problem has been hanging on this life-saver raft of the good offices of the secretary-general for the past 34 years. We need it (his good offices) to continue."
"Cyprus is not a Greek Cypriot Republic. Greek Cypriots hae no right under the rule of law to represent the whole island," he said.
"The European Union, the champion of human rights disregards all these things."
Denktash suggested he had been trapped into coming to Glion, which is above Montreux along Lake Geneva.
He said he had wanted to pull out of the July talks in New York but he was told that the Swiss talks would only be general discussions on the Cyprus problem.
"I came but I made no secret of the fact that we would not talk if the EU starts negotiating with Cyprus," he said.
